title: Lamb's problem: Rayleigh surface wave from a line force on a half-space (analytic)
description:
A downward line force on the free surface of an elastic half-space (nu = 1/4: cL = sqrt(3) cS, cS = 3000 m/s, rho 2700; 3 shear wavelengths of solid over a 100-cell absorbing layer, 2 vacuum cells above it with a rigid y_hi face behind them, absorbing x faces; 50 cells per shear wavelength at f0). The force is a gaussian pulse (sin carrier at f0 = 1 MHz under a gaussian envelope, relative bandwidth 0.3). The force_source sits in the vacuum cell above the surface and is split over its two y faces: the vacuum-vacuum face does not move, so half of it, F = force / 2, acts on the surface face itself (a traction F delta(x)); force = 2 F.
Analytic (Rayleigh pole of Lamb's 2D problem, frequency independent): the surface Rayleigh pulse does not decay with distance; for a downward F (per m of z), at x > 0: u_x = K_x (F / mu) s(t - x / cR), u_y = K_y (F / mu) H[s](t - x / cR), H the Hilbert transform, s the force waveform, cR = cS sqrt(2 - 2 / sqrt(3)) = 0.9194 cS; K = residues of the Rayleigh function r(s) = (2 s^2 - 1)^2 - 4 s^2 sqrt(s^2 - 1/3) sqrt(s^2 - 1) at s_R = cS / cR: K_x = (2 s_R^2 - 1) / (2 s_R r'(s_R)) = -1/8 (the static Flamant u_x = -(1 - 2 nu) F / (4 mu) after the pulse has passed), K_y = sqrt(s_R^2 - 1/3) / r'(s_R) = -0.1835 (|u_y / u_x| = 1.468, retrograde ellipse). Probes record v_y on the +y face of the top solid cell, i.e. on the surface (u_x would be read dx / 2 deep, where its steep depth profile changes it by ~15 %). For the narrow-band pulse H[s] = -envelope cos(w0 tau) (Bedrosian, error ~exp(-1 / bw^2) = 1e-5), so v_y = A (envelope (-w0 sin(w0 tau) - 2 tau / tau_g^2 cos(w0 tau))), A = -K_y F / mu. P and S contributions along the surface fall as (k r)^(-3/2) (< 1 % at 4 shear wavelengths).
Derived values tab: m1_matched / m2_matched = in-phase matched filters of v_y on the predicted Rayleigh pulse at 4 and 8 shear wavelengths, over its energy (1 expected; a Rayleigh speed error of 0.1 % costs ~0.3 % at probe 2, the shear speed instead of cR gives ~0); e1_energy / e2_energy = window energy of v_y over the predicted one (1 expected, insensitive to the arrival time: the amplitude check). Tolerance 5 % (the plan's estimate; the staggered-grid free surface has its own Rayleigh dispersion, so a phase-only miss shows as m < 1 with e ~ 1), to be confirmed by the first run.
Probes tab: probe_1 / probe_2 v_y with the dashed Rayleigh pulses (tolerance 5 % of the range) and the pulse at the shear speed (no tolerance).

parameters.name: f0
parameters.description: carrier frequency of the gaussian force pulse

parameters.name: bw
parameters.description: relative bandwidth of the pulse (narrow: H[s] = -envelope cos)

parameters.name: tau_g
parameters.description: 1/e half-width of the pulse envelope in s (1.06 us)

parameters.name: t0_g
parameters.description: time of the envelope maximum at the source in s

parameters.name: w0
parameters.description: angular carrier frequency in rad/s

parameters.name: rho_s
parameters.description: solid density in kg/m^3

parameters.name: cS_s
parameters.description: shear speed in m/s

parameters.name: cL_s
parameters.description: longitudinal speed in m/s (nu = 1/4)

parameters.name: mu_s
parameters.description: shear modulus in Pa

parameters.name: cR_s
parameters.description: Rayleigh speed in m/s (0.9194 cS = 2758)

parameters.name: sR2
parameters.description: s_R^2 = (cS / cR)^2

parameters.name: sR
parameters.description: s_R = cS / cR

parameters.name: aR
parameters.description: alpha / kS at the Rayleigh pole

parameters.name: bR
parameters.description: beta / kS at the Rayleigh pole

parameters.name: r_prime
parameters.description: derivative of the Rayleigh function at s_R (-5.024)

parameters.name: K_x
parameters.description: horizontal Rayleigh residue (-1/8; for reference, not measured)

parameters.name: K_y
parameters.description: vertical Rayleigh residue (-0.1835)

parameters.name: F_line
parameters.description: downward surface line force in N/m (the force_source gets 2 F, see the description)

parameters.name: A_uy
parameters.description: amplitude of the u_y Rayleigh pulse in m (7.6e-9)

parameters.name: dx_cell
parameters.description: uniform cell size (50 cells per shear wavelength, 60 um)

parameters.name: n_pml
parameters.description: absorbing layer cells on the x faces and y_lo (2 shear wavelengths)

parameters.name: Lx
parameters.description: domain length (54 mm)

parameters.name: y_surf
parameters.description: free surface (solid below, 2 vacuum cells above)

parameters.name: Ly
parameters.description: domain height

parameters.name: x_s
parameters.description: source x (cell centre, 3 shear wavelengths from the x_lo layer)

parameters.name: r1
parameters.description: probe 1 distance (4 shear wavelengths, 12 mm)

parameters.name: r2
parameters.description: probe 2 distance (8 shear wavelengths, 24 mm)

parameters.name: t_R1
parameters.description: Rayleigh pulse centre at probe 1 in s

parameters.name: t_R2
parameters.description: Rayleigh pulse centre at probe 2 in s

parameters.name: E_w
parameters.description: time integral of the squared predicted v_y pulse in m^2/s

parameters.name: S_courant
parameters.description: courant setting

parameters.name: T_run
parameters.description: study duration (probe 2's window ends at t_R2 + 3.5 tau_g)

derived_values.name: m1_matched
derived_values.expression: where(abs(t - t_R1) < 3.5*tau_g, values*A_uy*exp(-((t - t_R1)/tau_g)**2)*(-w0*sin(w0*(t - t_R1)) - 2*(t - t_R1)/tau_g**2*cos(w0*(t - t_R1))), 0)/E_w

derived_values.name: m2_matched
derived_values.expression: where(abs(t - t_R2) < 3.5*tau_g, values*A_uy*exp(-((t - t_R2)/tau_g)**2)*(-w0*sin(w0*(t - t_R2)) - 2*(t - t_R2)/tau_g**2*cos(w0*(t - t_R2))), 0)/E_w

analytic_curves.name: probe_2_at_cS
analytic_curves.expression: A_uy*exp(-((t - t0_g - r2/cS_s)/tau_g)**2)*(-w0*sin(w0*(t - t0_g - r2/cS_s)) - 2*(t - t0_g - r2/cS_s)/tau_g**2*cos(w0*(t - t0_g - r2/cS_s)))
